item.title: #3315265: Improve support of native MERGE with RETURNING merge_action()
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +466/−0 · php +466
  • Diff: 2c9c31c
  • Discussion: #3315265 · 4 contributors · 31 comments
  • Followers: 8
  • AI disclosures: 1 of 4 contributors

Summary

On PostgreSQL 18+ (the minimum for Drupal 12), Drupal's Merge query (the "insert or update" helper used by core's key_value store, the locale module's string location tracking, and the taxonomy index that is rebuilt whenever a published node is saved) now executes as a single native SQL MERGE statement instead of a SELECT followed by a separate INSERT or UPDATE. This halves the number of database round trips for these operations and also closes a small race-condition window that existed in the old check-then-write approach. There is no API change and nothing for site owners or module authors to configure; PostgreSQL sites simply get faster, safer merge queries automatically. Benchmarks in the issue showed 14 to 18% less time per merge query on a low-latency connection, with larger savings expected when there is more network latency between the web and database servers.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The PostgreSQL driver gets a new \Drupal\pgsql\Driver\Database\pgsql\Merge class, returned by the driver's Connection::merge(), which extends the generic \Drupal\Core\Database\Query\Merge. Its __toString() builds a MERGE INTO {table} USING (SELECT 1) AS drupal_merge_source ON (...) statement with WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE and WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT clauses, ending in RETURNING merge_action(). executeNativeMerge() binds all placeholders (including blob fields, expressions, and select-expression arguments) and maps the returned merge_action() value ('INSERT'/'UPDATE') back to Merge::STATUS_INSERT or Merge::STATUS_UPDATE, returning NULL when the row matched but no update fields were supplied.

isNativeMerge() gates when the native path is used: the condition must target the merge table itself and there must be insert fields or default fields. Otherwise execute() falls back to the parent's generic SELECT + INSERT/UPDATE emulation, specifically when the condition targets another table (no ON clause possible), when there are no insert fields (no WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT possible), or when values are inserted into serial fields, since the generic insert path also synchronizes the table's sequence afterwards.

Because native MERGE under PostgreSQL's default READ COMMITTED isolation is still subject to a race where a concurrent transaction inserts the same row between the match phase and the write, execute() catches IntegrityConstraintViolationException and retries the statement once, so the now-existing row is matched and updated instead. A new \Drupal\Tests\pgsql\Kernel\pgsql\MergeTest covers the native SQL string, single-statement execution, the no-update-match case, expressions, blob fields, and each fallback-to-emulation scenario.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">

item.title: #3615415: Remove using preg_replace() on every query for PostgreSQL
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Major task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 8 files, +206/−16 · php +206/−16
  • Diff: f0a5223
  • Discussion: #3615415 · 4 contributors · 17 comments
  • Followers: 5
  • AI disclosures: 2 of 4 contributors

Summary

On PostgreSQL, every single database query used to be passed through a preg_replace() call looking for LIKE and regular-expression operators so it could add a ::text type-cast to the field they act on (PostgreSQL doesn't auto-cast non-text columns for those operators). That regex ran on every query regardless of whether it used those operators, and it worked over the final SQL string so it could also mismatch inside expressions or string literals. This change moves the cast into query compilation, so it is only added to the specific conditions that need it, removing the per-query overhead for the many queries that never use LIKE or regex operators. Raw SQL strings (not built with the query builder) still get the old rewrite as a fallback, but relying on that is now deprecated since it will be removed in Drupal 13.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: The array returned by Connection::mapConditionOperator() supports a new field_suffix key that Condition::compile() appends to the field before the operator; database drivers overriding the condition operator map should be aware of it.
  • Deprecation: Relying on the PostgreSQL driver's Connection::prepareStatement() to auto-add a ::text cast to fields used with LIKE/regex operators in raw SQL strings is deprecated in drupal:11.5.0 and removed in drupal:13.0.0.
  • New API: New public method Connection::getConditionFieldSuffix() returns the SQL suffix (e.g. a type-cast) a driver needs appended to a field for a given condition operator, for use when building raw SQL condition snippets.

Technical details

Condition::compile() now supports a field_suffix directive in the array returned by Connection::mapConditionOperator(), appended to the compiled field fragment before the operator. The PostgreSQL driver's $postgresqlConditionOperatorMap sets 'field_suffix' => '::text' for LIKE, LIKE BINARY, NOT LIKE, REGEXP and NOT REGEXP, plus identity entries for ILIKE, NOT ILIKE, ~* and !~* so code (such as Views' StringFilter) that builds conditions with those PostgreSQL-native operators directly also gets the cast.

For code that builds raw SQL condition snippets outside the query builder (e.g. Query::where()), a new Connection::getConditionFieldSuffix($operator) method exposes the same suffix so it can be added manually. pgsql\Connection::prepareStatement() keeps its old preg_replace() fallback for raw SQL, but now guards it behind a stripos()/str_contains() check so it only runs for strings actually containing LIKE or ~*, made the regex idempotent (skips fields already cast), and raises an E_USER_DEPRECATED notice when it rewrites a query, pointing at the change record for removal in Drupal 13. StringFilter's operator handlers (opEqual, opContains, opStartsWith, opEndsWith, opNotLike, opRegex, etc.) were updated to call getConditionFieldSuffix() and append it to the expression themselves, since they build raw where-expression snippets rather than using Condition::compile().

Upgrade

Custom database drivers that override mapConditionOperator() can add a field_suffix entry to have it appended to the field automatically during condition compilation.

Code that issues raw SQL strings against PostgreSQL using LIKE, NOT LIKE, ILIKE, REGEXP, or ~*/!~* should add the cast explicitly instead of relying on the driver to rewrite the query, since that fallback is deprecated and removed in Drupal 13:

$suffix = $connection->getConditionFieldSuffix('LIKE');
$query->where("[title]$suffix LIKE :pattern", [
  ':pattern' => '%foo%',
]);

item.title: #3585455: Fix return types and baselined errors of core/tests/ Unit code - round 6
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 80 files, +346/−1371 · php +345/−1371 · dist +1
  • Diff: 4ef3e3b
  • Discussion: #3585455 · 5 contributors · 30 comments
  • Followers: 6
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 5 contributors

Summary

This is round 6, and the final round, of a series adding explicit PHP return type declarations across Drupal core's test code (core/tests/) and cleaning up the corresponding PHPStan baseline suppressions. It is almost entirely internal test tooling, but it does add return types to several widely used, subclassable test helper methods, most notably on BrowserTestBase, UiHelperTrait, SessionTestTrait, and DrupalTestBrowser, the base classes and traits that essentially every functional test in Drupal core and contributed modules extends or uses. Custom test code that overrides the affected methods without matching return types will fail with a fatal PHP error after this change.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Protected methods on UiHelperTrait, SessionTestTrait, DrupalTestBrowser, and BrowserTestBase (the base for nearly all Drupal functional tests) gained explicit return types, e.g. submitForm(), drupalLogin(), drupalLogout(), click(), clickLink(), prepareRequest(), generateSessionName(): void, and getTextContent(), getSessionName(): string.

Technical details

Most of the diff removes now-obsolete $ignoreErrors[] entries from core/.phpstan-baseline.php that were suppressing missingType.return and related identifiers, with the fixes landing in the corresponding test files: adding : void, : string, or other return types to methods, typing class properties (e.g. protected int $timeLimit, protected ?Mink $mink, protected string $sessionName), and a few unrelated small fixes surfaced by stricter typing.

The most consequential changes are in core/tests/Drupal/Tests/UiHelperTrait.php, SessionTestTrait.php, DrupalTestBrowser.php, and BrowserTestBase.php, which back nearly all functional testing in Drupal: submitForm(), drupalLogin(), drupalLogout(), prepareRequest(), click(), clickLink(), and generateSessionName() now return void, and getTextContent()/getSessionName() now return string. Typing BrowserTestBase::$mink as ?Mink (previously untyped, defaulting to implicit NULL) also required changing if ($this->mink) to if (isset($this->mink)) in tearDown(), since accessing an uninitialized typed property throws rather than evaluating falsy.

Outside core/tests/, the only production code touched is a docblock precision improvement on ArgumentsResolver::$objects (@var array to @var array<string,object>), and core/phpstan.neon.dist gained an additional excluded path for Doctrine annotation fixtures. Everything else (core/tests/Drupal/Tests/Core/*, Component/*, Composer/*) is internal unit test code not intended for external reuse. Related prior rounds: #3551596, #3562361, #3562868, #3562645, and #3579189 (Kernel tests), the last of which similarly touched a shared KernelTestBase/AssertContentTrait surface.

Upgrade

If a custom test class overrides any of these methods, add a matching return type:

// Before
protected function submitForm(array $edit, $submit, $form_html_id = NULL) { ... }
protected function drupalLogin(AccountInterface $account) { ... }
protected function click(string $css_selector) { ... }

// After
protected function submitForm(array $edit, $submit, $form_html_id = NULL): void { ... }
protected function drupalLogin(AccountInterface $account): void { ... }
protected function click(string $css_selector): void { ... }

The same applies to drupalLogout(), prepareRequest(), clickLink(), and generateSessionName() (all void), and getTextContent()/getSessionName() (string).

  • Committed: September 3, 2026 (4 months later)

item.title: #3555916: Update to htmx 4
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Critical task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 38 files, +1091/−742 · php +716/−527 · js +333/−176 · yml +34/−33 · lock +7/−5 · json +1/−1
  • Diff: 2aa5aed
  • Discussion: #3555916 · 8 contributors · 111 comments
  • Followers: 16
  • AI disclosures: 1 of 8 contributors

Summary

Drupal core's bundled HTMX library has been upgraded from version 2 to the newly released version 4, which the HTMX project describes as a complete rewrite ("the fetch()ening"). Core's HTMX integration (the PHP Htmx attribute-builder class, the request-header helpers, FormBuilder's HTMX handling, and the client-side JavaScript that wires HTMX into Drupal's AJAX/behavior system) has been refactored to work with the new library. There are no visible UI changes for standard core usage, but sites with custom code, themes, or contrib modules that use HTMX attributes, HTMX request/response headers, or HTMX JavaScript extensions should review the published change record, since htmx 4 changes attribute names, header names and formats, event payloads, the extension registration API, and introduces a default 60 second request timeout and different history/back-navigation behavior.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Requirements: The bundled htmx.js/htmx.min.js vendor library is upgraded from 2.0.4 to 4.0.0, a rewrite with backward-incompatible changes to attributes, headers, events, and the extension API.
  • API change: The Drupal\Core\Htmx\Htmx factory class was substantially reworked for htmx 4: several methods were renamed or removed (e.g. disable()→ignore(), disabledElt()→disable(), request()→config(); ext(), disinherit(), history(), inherit(), params(), and prompt() were removed because those attributes no longer exist in htmx 4), most builder methods gained an int $modifiers parameter for the new :inherited/:append attribute modifiers, and new methods action(), method(), query(), and status() were added for new htmx 4 attributes. HtmxRequestInfoTrait methods were renamed to match new/changed HTMX headers: getHtmxTrigger() and getHtmxPrompt() are gone, getHtmxTriggerName() now parses the triggering element's name out of the new HX-Source header, and a new getHtmxRequestType() reads the HX-Request-Type header.
  • Deprecation: FormBuilderInterface::HTMX_REQUEST constant is deprecated in favor of HtmxRequestInfoTrait::isHtmxRequest().

Technical details

The core-side changes track htmx 4's rewrite closely. HtmxRequestInfoTrait was updated because htmx 4 replaces the old HX-Trigger/HX-Trigger-Name headers with HX-Source (a CSS-selector-like identifier for the triggering element, URI-encoded) and adds HX-Request-Type ("full" or "partial"); getHtmxTriggerName() now regex-extracts a name="..." fragment out of HX-Source instead of reading a dedicated header. FormBuilder::prepareForm() had a latent bug here: it still read the removed hx-trigger header directly (rather than through the trait), which meant $hx_trigger was always NULL and the out-of-band form_build_id swap fired unconditionally; this was caught during review and fixed to use getHtmxSource()/getHtmxTarget() via the newly-added HtmxRequestInfoTrait usage in FormBuilder.

The Htmx class (core/lib/Drupal/Core/Htmx/Htmx.php) gained self::INHERITED/self::APPEND bit-flag modifiers, threaded through nearly every builder method via a new keyWithModifiers() helper, to support htmx 4's explicit :inherited/:append attribute-inheritance syntax. Several methods for attributes htmx 4 removed (ext, disinherit, history, inherit, params, prompt) were removed outright, others were renamed to match new attribute names (disable()→ignore(), disabledElt()→disable(), request()→config()), and new methods (action(), method(), query(), status()) were added for htmx 4's new hx-action, hx-method, hx-query (supporting the HTTP QUERY method), and hx-status attributes. Deprecation shims for the removed/renamed methods were left to a follow-up issue rather than being part of this change.

On the client, core/misc/htmx/htmx-assets.js was rewritten to hook into htmx 4's new event/task model: Drupal.attachBehaviors/detachBehaviors are now triggered from htmx:before:swap/htmx:after:swap handlers that resolve the correct DOM context from the swap task's target rather than the old htmx:beforeSwap/htmx:afterSettle events. core/core.libraries.yml now aggregates the htmx asset and points at v4.0.0. FormBuilderInterface::HTMX_REQUEST is marked @deprecated in favor of HtmxRequestInfoTrait::isHtmxRequest().

Upgrade

Review the published HTMX 4 change record for the full list of breaking changes. In particular, if custom or contrib code:

  • Calls removed Htmx methods, replace them, e.g.:
// Before
(new Htmx())->request(['timeout' => 5000]);
// After
(new Htmx())->config(['timeout' => 5000]);
  • Reads the old HTMX request headers directly, switch to the trait or the new header names (HX-Trigger/HX-Trigger-Name are gone, use HX-Source/HX-Request-Type).
  • Listens for Drupal's custom htmx:drupal:load/htmx:drupal:unload events, note the event payload shape may differ since it now derives its target from the htmx 4 swap task queue.
  • Registers an HTMX extension, htmx 4 replaces htmx.defineExtension() with htmx.registerExtension(name, extension) and a flat hook-object shape.

Also account for the new default 60 second request timeout and the change to no-DOM-cache history/back-navigation behavior in htmx 4.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: November 4, 2025
  • Committed: September 3, 2026 (10 months later)

Key contributors

  • nod_ (Très Bien Tech)
  • fathershawn (Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center)
  • catch (Third and Grove)
  • longwave (Full Fat Things)
  • godotislate
  • smustgrave (Mobomo)
  • cosmicdreams
  • latent

Collaboration

This nine-month effort was driven largely by fathershawn, who repeatedly rebased the branch through multiple htmx 4 beta releases (beta2 through beta6 and finally the 4.0.0 stable release) as the upstream API kept shifting, and who coordinated directly with htmx maintainers (including latent, credited with an assist on the swap/extension code) to resolve an upstream htmx bug where outerHTML swaps against a full-document response corrupted target attributes; the htmx team fixed it upstream after the discussion here. cosmicdreams did a close technical review that caught a real regression: FormBuilder still read the removed hx-trigger header, making its out-of-band form_build_id swap fire unconditionally, and separately flagged that Drupal's own htmx:drupal:load/htmx:drupal:unload custom events changed payload shape (detail.elt to target) without any upstream documentation to flag it, which fathershawn folded into the change record. longwave, catch, and others pushed to land the upgrade on main early despite htmx 4 still being in beta, reasoning it was safer to ride htmx 4's betas toward Drupal 12 than to release Drupal 12 locked to htmx 2 for years; catch's comment framed this directly given "HTMX has never had, and never will have, a version 3."

item.title: #3583153: Allow to invoke multiple implementations of a specific module with ModuleHandler::invoke()
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 5 files, +151/−1 · php +144/−1 · yml +7
  • Diff: 1b4da6d
  • Discussion: #3583153 · 6 contributors · 23 comments
  • Followers: 9
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 6 contributors

Summary

Previously, calling ModuleHandler::invoke() to run a specific hook for a specific module would throw a LogicException as soon as that module had more than one implementation of the hook, regardless of what those implementations returned. This forced developers to fall back on the more awkward invokeAllWith() just to support a module with multiple hook implementations. Now, invoke() runs all of that module's implementations and merges their results when possible, so code that only needs array results (the common case) works without extra workarounds. The exception is now only raised when the implementations return something that cannot be merged, such as strings or plain objects.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: ModuleHandler::invoke() no longer always throws when a module implements the same hook more than once: if every implementation returns NULL, an array, or an \ArrayObject, the results are merged with NestedArray::mergeDeep() and returned; it still throws \LogicException only when a non-mergeable value (e.g. a string or object) is returned.

Technical details

In ModuleHandler::invoke(), the branch handling multiple listeners for a module/hook pair (Drupal\Core\Extension\ModuleHandler::invoke()) no longer throws immediately on count($listeners) > 1. Instead it iterates the listeners, skips any that return NULL, and merges array or \ArrayObject results together with NestedArray::mergeDeep(). If a listener returns any other type, the original \LogicException ("Module $module should not implement $hook more than once.") is thrown instead, preserving the old failure mode for non-mergeable results. The interface doc comment on ModuleHandlerInterface::invoke() was updated to document this merging behavior.

A new hidden test module, hook_single_invoke, was added with hook implementations that return arrays, \ArrayObjects, strings, and stdClass objects, used by new tests (testInvokeWithMergeable(), testInvokeWithNotMergeableString(), testInvokeWithNotMergeableClass()) covering both the merge path and the exception path.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: April 5, 2026
  • Committed: September 2, 2026 (5 months and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • nicxvan (nLightened Development LLC)
  • berdir (MD Systems GmbH)
  • smustgrave (Mobomo)
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)
  • amateescu

Collaboration

berdir framed the design decision early in the issue, proposing that invoke() should only throw when results genuinely can't be merged rather than whenever a module has more than one implementation, noting that the ultimate_cron contrib module was running into this limitation (see #3501360) and that the change would let it drop its workaround pattern.

item.title: #3375423: Deprecate file_managed_file_save_upload(), file_save_upload() and _file_save_upload_from_form() and replace with a service
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 18 files, +433/−228 · php +431/−228 · yml +2
  • Diff: e842449
  • Discussion: #3375423 · 9 contributors · 72 comments
  • Followers: 24
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 9 contributors

Summary

Three long-standing procedural functions for handling file uploads from forms, file_save_upload(), file_managed_file_save_upload(), and _file_save_upload_from_form(), are now deprecated in favor of two new services. The functions still work exactly as before (they now just delegate internally), so no behavior changes for site visitors, but any custom code calling them directly will start seeing deprecation notices and must be updated ahead of the Drupal 13.0.0 removal.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: Procedural functions file_save_upload(), file_managed_file_save_upload(), and _file_save_upload_from_form() are deprecated in drupal:11.5.0 and removed in drupal:13.0.0, replaced by the Drupal\file\Upload\FormFileUploader and Drupal\file\Upload\ManagedFileElementHelper services.

Technical details

The old code mixed API-level file handling with Form API concerns (setting form errors, adding/removing Messenger messages, rendering error lists) in the same functions, which made the logic hard to reuse or test in isolation. This part of the broader #3221796 modernization effort splits that responsibility into two services.

Drupal\file\Upload\FormFileUploader::saveFormUploadedFiles() replaces file_save_upload(). It is the API-level entry point: it pulls uploaded files via UploadedFilesExtractor, delegates the actual move/validate/rename work to FileUploadHandlerInterface::handleFileUpload(), and caches results per form field in the cache.memory bin (keyed file:uploads:<field_name>) instead of the old function-static $upload_cache, so repeated calls within a request return the same result without reprocessing. It still calls \Drupal::messenger()->addError() directly on failure rather than being fully decoupled from user-facing messaging; a follow-up to remove that was tried and then reverted (see #3619417) to keep this change scoped.

Drupal\file\Upload\ManagedFileElementHelper replaces file_managed_file_save_upload() and _file_save_upload_from_form(). It owns the Messenger and Renderer dependencies, handling the form-level concerns: collecting per-field validation errors into a single FormStateInterface::setError() call, preserving pre-existing error messages, and calling into FormFileUploader for the actual upload. Drupal\file\Element\ManagedFile::valueCallback() and other core callers (ThemeSettingsForm, SystemBrandingOffCanvasForm, navigation's logo settings, and file access checks) were updated to call these services directly. Both services are registered in file.services.yml.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">Replace direct calls to the deprecated functions with the new services:

// Before:
$file = file_save_upload($form_field_name, $validators, $destination, $delta, $fileExists);
// After:
$file = \Drupal::service(\Drupal\file\Upload\FormFileUploader::class)
  ->saveFormUploadedFiles($form_field_name, $validators, $destination, $delta, $fileExists);

// Before:
$files = file_managed_file_save_upload($element, $form_state);
// After:
$files = \Drupal::service(\Drupal\file\Upload\ManagedFileElementHelper::class)
  ->managedFileSaveUpload($element, $form_state);

// Before:
$result = _file_save_upload_from_form($element, $form_state, $delta, $fileExists);
// After:
$result = \Drupal::service(\Drupal\file\Upload\ManagedFileElementHelper::class)
  ->saveFileUploads($element, $form_state, $delta, $fileExists);

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: July 19, 2023
  • Committed: September 1, 2026 (3 years and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • andypost (Skilld)
  • larowlan (PreviousNext)
  • smustgrave (Mobomo)
  • joachim (Factorial.io)
  • alexpott (Acro Commerce)
  • kim.pepper (PreviousNext)
  • nicxvan (nLightened Development LLC)
  • amateescu

Collaboration

This task stalled for a long time because of scope concerns. After an initial 2023 patch, alexpott pushed back in 2024 that the change was "doing more than it should", adding type hints that widened the BC surface and touching "logic deep in security focussed code" unnecessarily for what the issue set out to do. That comment effectively froze the issue for over a year. In 2025 kim.pepper concluded the issue had stalled "because it was trying to do too much" and proposed splitting it into several smaller, independently reviewable sub-issues (#3619416 through #3619420). Before that split was finished, nicxvan produced a full working MR overnight; kim.pepper reviewed it, renamed FileElementHelper to ManagedFileElementHelper to avoid confusion with existing render elements, and adjusted the cache scoping. The two then went back and forth on whether FormFileUploader should drop its Messenger/Renderer usage entirely: kim.pepper added FileUploadResult::addError()/getErrors() to make it possible, nicxvan judged that out of scope for this issue and reverted it into the follow-up #3619417, deferring the full decoupling rather than let it block this deprecation task.

item.title: #3549134: Move text_with_summary to its own module
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 35 files, +1210/−179 · php +1057/−119 · yml +77/−60 · js +76
  • Diff: daa6678
  • Discussion: #3549134 · 11 contributors · 58 comments
  • Followers: 12
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 11 contributors

Summary

Drupal's long-deprecated "Text (formatted, long, with summary)" field type is being carved out of the core text module into its own dedicated, deprecated text_with_summary module, as the final step of removing it from core ahead of Drupal 12. Existing sites that already use this field type (most commonly the body field on nodes) are automatically migrated: an update hook installs the new text_with_summary module when any field of that type is detected, and follow-up update hooks repoint the module dependency on the affected field storage, field, form display, and view display configuration from text to text_with_summary. No manual action is required for a normal update; the field, its data, and its "Summary or trimmed" display option keep working exactly as before.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: text_with_summary field type/formatter/widget classes in the text module (TextWithSummaryItem, TextSummaryOrTrimmedFormatter, TextareaWithSummaryWidget) are deprecated in Drupal 11.5.0 and removed in Drupal 12.0.0; use the equivalent classes in the new text_with_summary module instead. The drupal.text asset library in text.module is deprecated the same way.

Technical details

The field type plugin (TextWithSummaryItem), its widget (TextareaWithSummaryWidget), the text_summary_or_trimmed formatter, the associated JS behavior (js/text.js, the summary show/hide toggle), and the corresponding field.field_settings.text_with_summary/field.value.text_with_summary/field.widget.settings.text_textarea_with_summary/field.formatter.settings.text_summary_or_trimmed schema all move into the new core/modules/text_with_summary module (lifecycle: deprecated, depends on drupal:text). The old classes remain in text as thin, @deprecated shims pointing to their text_with_summary counterparts (see #3568381), and TextTrimmedFormatter gained a protected addTrimPreRender() helper so both the text module's own text_trimmed formatter and the new module's text_summary_or_trimmed formatter can share the trimming logic without one depending on the other's field type.

Because text_with_summary depends on text rather than the reverse, text_with_summary uses hook_field_formatter_info_alter() to re-register the text_with_summary field type against text's text_default/text_trimmed formatters, and hook_library_info_alter() to make the text module's drupal.text library (now empty and marked deprecated in text.libraries.yml) depend on text_with_summary/drupal.text, which carries the actual JS.

The migration path lives in text.install's text_update_12001(), which installs text_with_summary only if a field_storage_config of type text_with_summary exists, followed by post-update hooks (text_post_update_update_field_storage_dependencies, ..._field_dependencies, ..._form_display_dependencies, ..._view_display_dependencies, ..._view_dependencies) that use ConfigEntityUpdater to flip the recorded module dependency from text to text_with_summary on each affected config entity. Summary

This issue deprecates fourteen of those constants in favor of PHP backed enums and class constants, with no functional change to how translation import, update checking, or the translation settings form behave. Site owners see no change; custom code or contrib modules that reference the old constants directly will start seeing deprecation notices and need to update before Drupal 13.0.0, when the constants are removed.

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The constants are replaced according to a fixed mapping: LOCALE_NOT_CUSTOMIZED/LOCALE_CUSTOMIZED become LocaleDefaultOptions::NOT_CUSTOMIZED/LocaleDefaultOptions::CUSTOMIZED; LOCALE_TRANSLATION_USE_SOURCE_LOCAL/LOCALE_TRANSLATION_USE_SOURCE_REMOTE_AND_LOCAL become \Drupal\locale\Model\TranslationUpdateMode::Local/::RemoteAndLocal (both backed by string values, use ->value where a string is expected); LOCALE_TRANSLATION_OVERWRITE_ALL/_NON_CUSTOMIZED/_NONE become \Drupal\locale\Model\Overwrite::All/::NonCustomized/::None; and LOCALE_TRANSLATION_REMOTE/_LOCAL/_CURRENT become \Drupal\locale\Model\SourceType::Remote/::Local/::Current. Callers such as LocaleFetch, LocaleSource, LocaleProjectChecker and TranslationStatusForm were updated to use these helpers instead of comparing against the old constants or indexing $source->files[LOCALE_TRANSLATION_LOCAL] directly. item.title: #3616645: Form #value_callback does not support CallableResolver-style callables
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task

Summary

Form elements can now define their #value_callback using the same "service notation" already supported by #process, #after_build, #submit, #validate, and #entity_builders. Previously #value_callback only accepted plain PHP callables (functions, static methods, or [$object, 'method'] arrays); it could not point to a method on a class resolved through the service container, so it could not use constructor-injected dependencies. This unblocks converting existing static value callback methods, such as those used by file upload widgets, into injectable services.

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: #value_callback on form elements can now be defined in CallableResolver service notation (e.g. MyService:method), not just plain is_callable() values.

Technical details

FormBuilder::handleInputElement() previously read #value_callback directly and fell back to \Drupal\Core\Render\Element\FormElementBase::valueCallback only when the given value was not is_callable(). It now always resolves the callback through CallableResolver::getCallableFromDefinition(), after passing it through FormStateInterface::prepareCallback() (the same pipeline used for #process and #after_build), so definitions like MyClass:method or a service id with a method are resolved via the class resolver/container instead of requiring a directly callable value. Plain static and array callables continue to resolve the same way, since CallableResolver falls back to normal PHP callable resolution when the definition is already callable. An unresolvable definition now throws \InvalidArgumentException instead of silently falling back to the default value callback, as covered by the new testValueCallbackInvalidDefinitionThrows() kernel test. This change removes a blocker for #3616654, which converts ManagedFile::valueCallback() into an injectable service, part of the file upload modernization tracked in the meta issue #3221796.

Existing #value_callback definitions (plain functions, static method strings, or [$object, 'method'] arrays) keep working unchanged. To use dependency injection, define the callback in service notation, for example:

$element['#value_callback'] = MyValueCallbackService::class . ':value';

which is then resolved through CallableResolver the same way #process and #submit callbacks already are.

update_get_available($refresh);
// After:
\Drupal::service(\Drupal\update\UpdateManagerInterface::class)->getAvailable($refresh);

// Before:
update_create_fetch_task($project);
// After:

// After:

item.description:

  • Type: Normal bug report

Summary

On sites using core's experimental default_admin theme, visiting admin pages built from Views status fields (such as /admin/people) triggered a PHP 8.5 deprecation warning, "Using null as an array offset is deprecated", because the "Published"/"Unpublished" badge template tried to look up a translation using a language code that could be null. The same faulty logic also meant the published/unpublished badge could show the wrong color on views not based on nodes (for example taxonomy term listings), since it relied on a variable that only exists for node-based views. Both problems are fixed: the warning no longer appears, and the badge now reflects the correct publication state for any publishable entity type shown in a status field.

Impact

Affects front-end developers.

  • Theme change: The default_admin theme's views-view-field--status.html.twig template no longer resolves the row's translated entity itself; it now receives a computed is_published boolean/null variable from a new preprocess hook, and no longer receives an entity variable.

Technical details

The old views-view-field--status.html.twig template inlined Twig logic to fetch the row's entity translation via row._entity.getTranslation(row.node_field_data_langcode) before checking isPublished(). node_field_data_langcode is a row property that only exists for node-based views, so on other views (or monolingual sites) it evaluated to NULL, which is what triggered the deprecation inside ContentEntityBase::hasTranslation(), and also silently produced the wrong publication state for non-node entities like taxonomy terms.

The fix moves this logic out of the template entirely. A new hook_preprocess_HOOK() implementation, PreprocessHooks::preprocessViewsViewFieldStatus() (theme suggestion views_view_field__status, which fires for any views field with the machine ID status on any entity type), resolves the row's entity through the field handler's own EntityField::getEntity() (respecting configured relationships via row._relationship_entities), and only sets a boolean is_published variable when the field's underlying entity field type is boolean. Otherwise is_published is NULL. The template was simplified to branch purely on is_published: TRUE renders the marker--published span, FALSE renders the plain marker span, and NULL renders the raw output with no marker at all, so fields that aren't a real published flag (e.g. views_test_data.status handled by the boolean plugin) pass through unaffected.

Because the entity is now resolved through the field handler, translation handling follows the view's configured rendering language instead of a hardcoded node-specific row property, fixing the mismatch for non-node views. Follow-up issues #3608223 and #3619121 were opened to move this kind of status-badge formatting into a proper Views field formatter rather than being hardcoded in the theme layer.

Upgrade

Themes that override core/themes/default_admin/templates/views/views-view-field--status.html.twig need to update their copy: the template no longer receives an entity variable and instead receives is_published (TRUE, FALSE, or NULL):

{% if is_published is null %}
  {{ output -}}
{% elseif is_published %}
  <span class="marker marker--published">{{ output -}}</span>
{% else %}
  <span class="marker">{{ output -}}</span>
{% endif %}

Summary

Drupal has deprecated the long-standing procedural functions user_login_finalize() and user_logout() in favour of two new services. Logging a user in or out still works exactly the same way for site visitors; this change is about how module code performs those actions. Any custom or contributor code that calls these functions directly will keep working but will trigger a deprecation notice, and should switch to the new services before Drupal 13.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: user_login_finalize() and user_logout() are deprecated in drupal:11.5.0 and will be removed in drupal:13.0.0; use the new LoginFinalizer/LogoutFinalizer services instead.
  • New API: New final services Drupal\user\LoginFinalizer (finalizeLogin()) and Drupal\user\LogoutFinalizer (finalizeLogout()) registered in user.services.yml.

Technical details

The procedural logic previously living in user_login_finalize() and user_logout() (session regeneration, updating the last-login timestamp, invoking hook_user_login()/hook_user_logout(), destroying the session, and logging) has been moved verbatim into two new final readonly classes, Drupal\user\LoginFinalizer::finalizeLogin() and Drupal\user\LogoutFinalizer::finalizeLogout(). Both are plain services (no interfaces: an interface was originally proposed but dropped after berdir questioned the need for a swappable API with no known use case) declared in user.services.yml. The old functions now just emit an E_USER_DEPRECATED notice and delegate to the new services.

All core call sites were switched to constructor-injected dependencies instead of calling the global functions: UserAuthenticationController, UserController, UserLoginForm, UserLogoutConfirm, RegisterForm, and install.core.inc. Each affected constructor gained new optional LoginFinalizer/LogoutFinalizer parameters defaulting to NULL, with a deprecation notice thrown when omitted so that existing subclasses keep working until the parameter becomes required. MaintenanceModeSubscriber, which runs on every request, injects the logout service lazily via #[AutowireServiceClosure(LogoutFinalizer::class)] rather than eagerly resolving it in the constructor.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">Replace direct calls to the deprecated functions:

// Before
user_login_finalize($account);
user_logout();

// After
\Drupal::service(\Drupal\user\LoginFinalizer::class)->finalizeLogin($account);
\Drupal::service(\Drupal\user\LogoutFinalizer::class)->finalizeLogout();

Prefer constructor injection of Drupal\user\LoginFinalizer and/or Drupal\user\LogoutFinalizer where possible.

If you subclass UserAuthenticationController, UserController, UserLoginForm, UserLogoutConfirm, or RegisterForm and call their constructors directly, pass the new $loginFinalizer/$logoutFinalizer arguments to avoid deprecation notices; they will become required in a future release.

item.title: #3610503: Optimize StorageCopyTrait::replaceStorageContents()
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +27/−14 · php +27/−14
  • Diff: 7230379
  • Discussion: #3610503 · 3 contributors · 19 comments
  • Followers: 4

Summary

Importing configuration (for example via drush config:import) used to read each changed config object from the database one at a time, which could mean hundreds or thousands of individual queries on a site with a large config set. This change batches those reads into chunks of 500, cutting the number of queries down to a handful. The issue author measured a couple hundred milliseconds saved on a Umami config import, with larger savings expected on sites with more configuration. Combined with the related config file parsing cache improvements in #3591680, this is expected to cut more than half the time off a typical drush config import.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The fix is in StorageCopyTrait::replaceStorageContents(), which is used whenever one config storage is synced into another (config import, config staging, etc.). Previously it looped over every config name and called $source_collection->read($name) and $target_collection->read($name) individually. Now it splits the list of names into array_chunk($names, 500) batches and calls readMultiple() once per chunk on both the source and target storage, then compares the in-memory arrays to decide whether to write or delete each item. For storage backends like DatabaseStorage, readMultiple() already issued a single SELECT ... WHERE name IN (...) query, so batching through it turns what could be thousands of round trips into a handful.

Making MemoryStorage::readMultiple() actually get exercised (it previously wasn't reachable from this code path) exposed a latent bug: it used array_intersect_key($this->config[$this->collection], array_flip($names)), which errors when the collection is empty or missing. It now delegates to read() per name, consistent with the class's other methods, which are only used in tests.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">

item.title: #3587797: Move views data cache to cache_discovery
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 4 files, +8/−19 · php +8/−19
  • Diff: 7d8143e
  • Discussion: #3587797 · 7 contributors · 40 comments
  • Followers: 10
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 7 contributors

Summary

Views builds a large in-memory data structure describing every database table exposed to Views (via hook_views_data()), and caches it both as one big entry and as many smaller per-table entries. Per-table entries were previously stored in the regular persistent cache (cache.default); they are now stored in the cache.discovery bin, which is chained with a fast, per-process backend like APCu when available. Since the set of tables is finite and rebuilt rarely, this lets repeat lookups for the same table on a page be served from local memory instead of the primary cache backend (Redis, database, etc.), reducing cache reads on pages that use Views. The single "all views data" entry stays in cache.default because it can be very large and the maintainers were concerned that pushing it into a fast in-memory bin could evict other cached data on large, multilingual sites.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: \Drupal\views\ViewsData::cacheGet() and cacheSet() are deprecated in Drupal 11.5.0 and removed in 12.0.0, with no replacement.

Technical details

The initial commit simply swapped the constructor's #[Autowire] target for ViewsData::$cacheBackend from cache.default to cache.discovery, but this was reverted after berdir pointed out that the combined "all tables" entry can be tens of megabytes on sites with many languages or entity bundles, and forcing all of that into the chained-fast (APCu-backed) bin risked frequent APCu expunges and a performance regression rather than an improvement.

The follow-up perf commit instead adds a second injected backend, $chainedFastBackend (cache.discovery), used only for the per-table cache entries in ViewsData::get(), while getData() keeps using $cacheBackend (cache.default) for the full "all tables" entry. A new ViewsData::CACHE_TAGS constant centralizes the views_data and config:core.extension cache tags used when setting either bin. The old protected cacheGet()/cacheSet() helpers, which always prefixed the langcode and used $cacheBackend, are no longer used internally and are deprecated with @trigger_error; callers should use the injected cache backends directly, following how the rest of the class now works.

Performance test fixtures (FrontPageTest, StandardPerformanceTestTrait, Umami/Standard profile test YAMLs) were updated to reflect the shift: discovery cache-get counts go up and default cache-get counts go down by the same amount, confirming per-table lookups now hit cache.discovery.

Upgrade

Subclasses or code relying on \Drupal\views\ViewsData::cacheGet() or cacheSet() will get a deprecation notice starting in Drupal 11.5.0 and must stop using them before 12.0.0, since there is no direct replacement method. Interact with the injected $cacheBackend (cache.default, for the "all data" entry) or the new $chainedFastBackend (cache.discovery, for per-table entries) directly instead:

// Before (deprecated):
$data = $this->cacheGet($cid);
$this->cacheSet($cid, $data);

// After, for per-table entries:
$data = $this->chainedFastBackend->get($this->prepareCid($cid));
$this->chainedFastBackend->set($this->prepareCid($cid), $data, Cache::PERMANENT, static::CACHE_TAGS);
